\section{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Orthogonality}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Orthogonality: Introduction}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Orthogonality: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of polynomial evaluations under Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_eval_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_eval_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_eval_gaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Every real polynomial is integrable under the standard Gaussian probability measure on
$\mathbb R$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial times Gaussian density is integrable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_standardGaussianPDF_mul_polynomial}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_standardGaussianPDF_mul_polynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_eval_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
For every real polynomial $p$, the function $x\mapsto\varphi(x)p(x)$ is integrable with
respect to Lebesgue measure, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Integration by Parts for Polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_polynomial_derivative_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_polynomial_derivative_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_standardGaussianPDF_mul_polynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
For every real polynomial $p$, integration against the standard Gaussian probability
measure $\gamma$ satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}p'(x)\,d\gamma(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}x p(x)\,d\gamma(x).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite Polynomial Integration by Parts]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_succ_mul_polynomial_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_succ_mul_polynomial_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_eval_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_polynomial_derivative_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
For every natural number $k$ and real polynomial $p$, integration against the standard
Gaussian measure satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb R} H_{k+1}(x)p(x)\,d\gamma(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}H_k(x)p'(x)\,d\gamma(x),
\]
where $H_m$ denotes the polynomial obtained by mapping the degree-$m$ Hermite polynomial
to real coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite integral and polynomial derivatives]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_mul_polynomial_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_mul_polynomial_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_succ_mul_polynomial_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a real polynomial. The standard Gaussian
integral of the degree-$k$ Hermite polynomial times $p$ equals the standard Gaussian
integral of the $k$th derivative of $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.iterate_derivative_hermite_self}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.iterate_derivative_hermite_self}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every integer $k\ge 0$, the $k$-fold iterated derivative of the degree-$k$ Hermite
polynomial is the constant polynomial with value $k!$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $j$ and $k$, the standard Gaussian integral of the product of the
degree-$j$ and degree-$k$ Hermite polynomials is $j!$ when $j=k$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Orthogonality of Normalized Hermite Polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_normalizedHermite_mul_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_normalizedHermite_mul_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermite_mul_hermite_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
For all natural numbers $j,k$, the normalized Hermite polynomials $H_j,H_k$ satisfy
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}H_j(x)H_k(x)\,d\gamma(x)=\begin{cases}1,&j=k,\\0,&j\ne k,\end{cases}
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Orthonormality of multivariate Hermite functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermiteFunction_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermiteFunction_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_eq_prod, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_normalizedHermite_mul_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\alpha,\beta:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$. The
integral of the product of their multivariate normalized Hermite functions against the
product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ is $1$ if $\alpha=\beta$, and $0$
otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Integration by Parts for Affine Polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_id_mul_polynomial_affine_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_id_mul_polynomial_affine_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_polynomial_derivative_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
For every real polynomial $p$ and all real numbers $a,b$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R} y\,p(a+by)\,d\gamma(y)=b\int_{\mathbb R}p'(a+by)\,d\gamma(y),
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a polynomial times an affine polynomial evaluation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_mul_affine_standardGaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_mul_affine_standardGaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_polynomial_eval_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p,q\in\mathbb R[X]$ and $a,b\in\mathbb R$. The function $y\mapsto q(y)p(a+by)$ is
integrable under the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$.
\end{lemma}
